# Deploying
Merge to main, then run the deploy pipeline. Watch the canary dashboard for ten minutes before promoting the release to every region.

## Rollback
If error rates climb, run the rollback job; it redeploys the previous build in about two minutes.

documents.description: What to do when something breaks
documents.content:
# Incident response
Page the on-call engineer through the pager rotation. Open an incident channel, name an incident commander, and post updates every thirty minutes until resolved.

## Postmortem
Write a blameless postmortem within five business days.

# Peach
Peach leads the Mushroom Kingdom. She approves budgets above ten thousand coins and chairs the Monday planning meeting.

# Mario
Mario owns the release checklist and the plumbing of the build system. Ask him about pipes, caching, and flaky tests.

# Luigi
Luigi runs customer support and the haunted mansion help desk. He triages tickets every morning.

# Toad
Toad keeps the castle's inventory: mushrooms, stars, and spare keys. He orders supplies on Fridays.
The castle gates open at dawn and close at dusk. Visitors sign in at the front desk.
The guest wifi network is MushroomGuest and the password rotates every Monday; the front desk has the current one.
The kitchen serves lunch from noon to two. Cake is baked every Sunday for the whole staff.
Customers are invoiced monthly in coins. Refunds above five hundred coins need Peach's approval.

# Database decision
We chose Postgres with the pgvector extension for memory search, over a separate vector database, to keep one source of truth.

# Pricing
From October the starter plan costs nine coins a month and the team plan forty coins per seat.
Never share the vault combination over chat. Rotate API keys every ninety days and store them in the secrets manager.
Staff request vacation in the HR portal at least two weeks ahead; Peach approves requests longer than a week.
Release notes are written in plain words, with the user-visible change first and the ticket number last.
